cinematic_beat_sequence_v2.print_copy: Across the Mountain Lake bridge, Wilson Look planted four hooves and raised his axe. “The Belt Keeper comes to ask permission?” he called. From the far landing, Austin Byars lifted his hooded head, red eyes burning in shadow. “Not yours,” came the answer. Behind Wilson, the carter held his horse and wagon still. Wilson made a mocking path between them. “After you, Austin.” The old lantern swung, the storm tore at their cloaks, and both warriors lowered their weapons. Neither intended to surrender the crossing. They charged.

folios.title: He was here before us
folios.concept: Professional-grade fight logic: impact -> pressure -> sidestep/pivot -> counterstrike -> visible hoof slip. Never invent airborne weapons, disconnected limbs or teleport.
folios.camera_and_composition: C (upper kinetic wedge): An over-shoulder charged contact: Wilson's axe comes down on a visible arc and Austin's ornate sword meets the haft/edge in one coherent plane; shower of sparks is brief and source-motivated. THEN D (central large image): Tracking reverse: Wilson rotates ALL FOUR hooves on wet central stones, uses body weight to press, Austin steps laterally toward lamp/reset stone, one boot planted, cloak trails leeward. Carter and cart remain at left approach. THEN E (lower diagonal payoff): Austin moves inside the axe reach, delivers a decisive armor-thudding sword strike across Wilson's upper guard; Wilson's hind hooves cross/skid and his front hooves scramble near the intact parapet, his body still on deck at cut.
folios.lighting_and_weather: Intense local storm squall: directional crosswind, whipping crimson cape and wagon canopy, leaves, cold rain, large wind-agitated waves hitting piers, loud whitecaps/spray beneath intact span.
folios.must_preserve_or_source: HMB never human-faced; Wilson FOUR equine hooves; constant bridge, lamp, carter and wave-loaded LAKE; Wilson is at edge with weight moving outward, all 4 hooves visible, still not in water; Austin sword held, Belt remains with Austin, bridge intact.

cinematic_beat_sequence_v2.print_copy: Their first collision rang against the lantern stones. Wilson drove his axe down; Austin caught its haft with his sword and turned aside instead of meeting the centaur’s weight head-on. Hooves hammered the narrow deck. Wilson twisted for a second cut, forcing Austin toward the parapet. “He was here before us,” Austin said, glancing at the waiting carter. He slipped inside the next swing and struck Wilson’s armored upper body. The impact shoved the huge warrior backward. His hind hooves crossed on rain-slick stone. All four feet fought for purchase as the parapet rushed toward him.

cinematic_beat_sequence_v2.print_copy: Austin’s final blow carried through the clash. Four hooves scraped for grip; Wilson’s enormous armored body pitched over the intact parapet and vanished into the raging, storm-churned water. The carter stopped breathing. Even Austin stepped to the edge, his gold belt still fixed at his waist. Waves battered the pier. Then Wilson’s dark head broke the foam—coughing, alive. Only when the great centaur reached toward shore did Austin release the small jester’s cap. “My jester,” he said, almost without triumph. His Majesty’s Blood 168.20 · D0nkey K0ng 129.75.

folios.title: Pick a side
folios.concept: Kevin Zeek stopped at the break in the vegetation. Rain had erased the easy-looking path, leaving roots slick and mud deep enough to steal a stride. Last week he had watched water undo his own defenses. He was not about to let Phillip see him hesitate. 'Race you to the dry stone.' Phillip Pitts turned all three heads toward the opening. 'You sure you want the short way?' Kevin grinned. 'I usually do.' He took the direct approach; Phillip followed the longer, firmer edge of the same visitor-side clearing.

folios.title: The dry stone
folios.concept: Kevin had the first few strides. Then the mud caught his foot and he had to steady himself against a root. Across the clearing Phillip kept moving, one head watching the ground, another tracking Kevin, the third fixed on the sheltered stone. When Kevin reached it, Phillip was already waiting. Kevin looked down at his muddy legs. 'You should see me on dry ground.' Phillip glanced at the stone beneath them. 'All three of us would love to.' Kevin laughed despite himself. The Snake had won on his own ground, 125.74 to 94.80.
